week0.title: Setup week
items: Book a doctor / rheumatologist visit: uric acid 8.2 with 2-3 flares a year - ask about urate-lowering medication (target < 6 mg/dL)
Book one golf lesson with a coach: swing check, priorities, and ask about your 7-iron launch (22°) and whether you add loft at impact
Ask the condo if a Pilates instructor can give you 1-2 intro sessions on the reformer
Set the SC4 at the net (ball ~10 ft from the net, unit ~5 ft behind the ball)
Tell your friend: no talking during swings in the money game
Decide your per-round loss cap and write it in the Rules tab of this tracker
Log today in the tracker - first check-in

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: Show up on schedule. Learn the movements. Install the routine. Get baseline numbers.
phases.body: Strength 3x/week at moderate effort: 2-3 sets of 10-12 reps, stop with 3-4 reps left. Easy cardio 30-40 min twice a week - one of them a swim. Mobility every day. Pilates reformer twice a week (Fri and Sun) for flexibility and core.
phases.golf: Pre-shot routine on every ball. Build your wedge distance chart. Putting start-line and lag work. Run the random-miss test in week 1.
phases.habits: Fixed wake time 7 days a week. Bedtime moves 15 min earlier each week. Drinks: max 3 nights a week in weeks 1-2, then max 2.

phases.name: Build
phases.goal: Get stronger and faster. Practise under pressure so the money game feels normal.
phases.body: Strength heavier: 3-4 sets of 6-8 reps, stop with 2-3 reps left. Add power work and speed sets (med-ball throws, kettlebell swings, low jumps). Cardio maintained. Pilates twice a week: add range in the rotation and hip exercises.
phases.golf: Noise drill and scored games every SC4 session. Course strategy plan for your home course. One SC4 simulator round a week using that plan.
phases.habits: Bedtime target 23:30, wake 07:30. Max 2 drinking nights, never the night before a round.

phases.name: Perform
phases.goal: Turn practice into scores. Fewer blow-up holes, steadier back nine.
phases.body: Maintain: 2 heavy strength days + 1 power day. Keep cardio for back-nine stamina. Pilates twice a week to keep the turn free.
phases.golf: Half of every SC4 session in play mode (new club and target every ball, full routine). Simulated betting rounds. On course, only targets from your strategy plan.
phases.habits: Hold the routine. Round-day protocol every time: sleep, water, no alcohol the night before.

tasks: Benchmark test #1 (SC4 + putting) - log it in Tests
Random-miss test: 10 x 7-iron normal, then 10 with phone playing chatter - compare direction spread
Body log: weight, waist
Strength at light weights - learn the movements
Fill the Clubs tab: average carry for every club - 10 normal swings each on the SC4, ignore the best 2 and worst 2, average the middle 6
SC4: carry for each wedge at 3 swing lengths (9 o'clock, 10:30, full) - write the chart
Putting: gate drill + lag drill each session
Doctor visit done?
Last 20 balls of every SC4 session: full pre-shot routine, new target each ball
Back-off rule: anything distracts you after setup - step away and restart
Add 1 rep or a little weight to each strength exercise
Strength: drop one set from each exercise
Putting test only (6 ft makes, 30 ft lag)
Review chat with Claude: what's working, what's not
Strength C adds med-ball throws, kettlebell swings, low box jumps
Speed set at the end of each SC4 full-swing session: 5 max-effort swings, log the top club speed
Noise drill in every SC4 session: someone talks or phone plays chatter - full routine, back off when needed
Strength A/B move to 6-8 reps, heavier
Build a hole-by-hole plan for your home course with Claude (target, club, danger side)
SC4 sim round on E6 using the plan
Wedge ladder scored game
Putting: 10 in a row from 4 ft (restart on miss)
SC4: 9-ball window test with 7-iron (score each ball in or out)
Put a small consequence on each game (e.g., 10 push-ups for a fail)
Benchmark test #2 (SC4 + putting) - compare with week 1
Body log + book uric acid re-test if on medication
Strength: drop one set from each exercise
Half of every SC4 session in play mode
Driver: track club speed every session
Strength: 2 heavy days + 1 power day
E6 sim round with a real (small) stake or consequence and chatter playing
Post-shot reset after every bad shot: 10 seconds, breath, re-grip, next
Review your round logs: front vs back nine
Round-day protocol on every round
Only strategy-plan targets on course
Keep strength and mobility going
Benchmark test #3 - compare with weeks 1 and 8
Body log: weight, waist, uric acid if re-tested
12-week review chat with Claude - set the next 12 weeks

Dumbbell bench press or push-up - 3 x 8-10||dumbbell bench press form
One-arm dumbbell row - 3 x 10 each side||one arm dumbbell row form
Half-kneeling cable chop - 3 x 10 each side||half kneeling cable chop
Half-kneeling cable lift - 3 x 10 each side||half kneeling cable lift

strC.title: Strength C - power + golf-specific
items: Warm-up: 5 min bike + hip and thoracic mobility
Med-ball rotational throw at a wall (or fast cable rotation) - 4 x 5 each side||medicine ball rotational throw golf
Kettlebell swing - 4 x 10||kettlebell swing proper form
Low box jump (weeks 1-4: step-ups) - 3 x 5||low box jump beginner
Single-leg Romanian deadlift - 3 x 8 each leg||single leg romanian deadlift form
Lateral lunge - 3 x 8 each side||lateral lunge form
Thoracic open books - 2 x 8 each side||thoracic open book stretch
strC.note: Power reps are fast and crisp. Stop the set when speed drops.

cardio.title: Mobility + easy cardio
items: Mobility flow (below) - 15 min
Incline walk, bike, rower or swim - 40 min at talk-but-not-sing pace (roughly 100-120 bpm)||zone 2 cardio explained

swim.title: Easy swim (25 m pool)
items: Outdoor pool: swim before 10:00 or after 16:00 (see Sun & UV rules)
Warm-up: 4 lengths (100 m) easy, any stroke
Main: 12-16 lengths (300-400 m) in 2-length repeats with 20-30 s rest - easy, steady breathing||freestyle swimming technique for adults
Mix freestyle and backstroke to balance the shoulders; go easy on breaststroke kick if your knees complain||backstroke technique beginner adults
Kick: 4 lengths with a kickboard (legs and hips)||kickboard drills freestyle
Cool-down: 2-4 lengths very easy
New to lap swimming? Start with 15-20 min and rest as needed, then add 2 lengths a week||lap swimming for beginners adults
swim.note: Swimming is easy on the joints and good for heart and recovery, but it doesn't replace the gym for muscle and bone. Stop if a shoulder hurts. Skip it during a gout flare, and drink water afterwards - you still sweat in the pool.

pilA.title: Pilates reformer A - core and hips
items: Footwork series (parallel, heels, toes, wide V) - 10 each, medium springs||reformer footwork series beginner
Bridging on the reformer - 10||reformer bridge beginner
Hundred with feet in tabletop - 5 rounds of 10 breaths||reformer hundred modified beginner
Leg circles in the straps - 8 each direction||reformer leg circles straps
Seated rowing, front and back - 8 each||reformer rowing series beginner
Elephant - 8||reformer elephant exercise
Knee stretches (round back, flat back) - 8 each||reformer knee stretch series
Mermaid side stretch - 4 each side||reformer mermaid stretch
pilA.note: New to the reformer? Book 1-2 sessions with a certified instructor to learn springs and straps safely. Light springs for stretches, medium for footwork. Skip footwork during a gout flare.

pilB.title: Pilates reformer B - rotation and flexibility
items: Footwork series - 10 each, light to medium springs||reformer footwork series beginner
Frog and leg lowers in the straps (hamstrings, hips) - 8 each||reformer frog leg lowers straps
Seated spine twist with a strap - 6 each side||reformer seated spine twist
Kneeling chest expansion - 8||reformer chest expansion kneeling
Swan on the long box (gentle back extension) - 6||reformer swan on box beginner
Side-lying leg series on the carriage - 8 each side||reformer side lying leg series
Hip-flexor lunge stretch on the carriage - 30 s each side||reformer lunge hip flexor stretch
Mermaid with twist - 4 each side||reformer mermaid twist
pilB.note: This is your flexibility session: thoracic rotation, hips and hamstrings are what let you turn fully in the backswing. Move slowly and breathe out on the effort.

items: Gate drill from 3 ft - 20 putts (start line)||putting gate drill

sc4w.title: SC4 - wedges and distance control
items: Warm-up - 10 easy wedges
Distance ladder: 30 / 50 / 70 / 90 / 110 yd carry, 5 balls each - aim within 5 yd||wedge distance ladder drill
Swing-length chart: each wedge at 9 o'clock, 10:30 and full - log the carries||wedge clock system distance control
Last 15 balls in play mode: new target every ball, full routine||random practice golf range

sc4f.title: SC4 - full swing
items: Warm-up - 10 balls
7-iron stock shot - 20 balls: launch direction within 3 degrees, watch carry spread||iron start line practice launch monitor
Driver - 15 balls if the net has room (otherwise 3-wood or hybrid): club speed, carry, launch direction||driver practice launch monitor
Coach drills from your last lesson
Speed set (from week 5): 5 max-effort swings with full rest - log the top club speed||golf speed training max effort swings
Last 20 balls in play mode: driver, iron, wedge like a real hole, full routine, back off if distracted||golf pre shot routine

round.title: Round-day protocol
items: Night before: no alcohol, no dramas, lights out by 22:00 for a 06:30 tee
Sun: SPF 50 PA++++ before you leave, reapply at the turn; hat, UV sunglasses, arm sleeves
500 ml water before the round, about 250 ml every 2-3 holes (more for an 11:00 tee)
Snack at the turn (banana, nuts) to protect the back nine
Pre-shot routine on every shot; back off if anyone talks||golf pre shot routine
Pick every approach club with the Clubs tab: average carry to the middle of the green; between clubs, take the longer one
Bogey is fine - take the safe side, no hero shots
Log the round in the tracker the same day, including approaches that finished short or long

tests.title: Benchmark test (weeks 1, 8, 12)
items: Driver - 10 swings with full routine (on the SC4 at the net if there's room, otherwise take the SC4 to a driving range): average club speed, average carry, launch direction spread (furthest left to furthest right)
7-iron - 10 swings: average club speed and ball speed, average carry, carry spread (longest minus shortest), direction spread
Wedge test - 3 balls each at 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 yd: within 5 yd = 2 points, within 10 yd = 1 point (max 24)
Putting - 10 putts from 6 ft (count makes) and 10 putts from 30 ft (count finishing inside 3 ft)

mind: Pre-shot routine: pick the target from behind the ball, one rehearsal swing, step in, look at the target twice, go. Same rhythm every time.
Back-off rule: if anyone talks or moves after you set up, step away and restart. Every time. No apology needed.
Post-shot reset: 10 seconds to react, then one slow breath, re-grip, and judge only whether you did your routine.
Before the money game: agree 'no talking during swings'. The Rules of Golf expect players not to distract someone making a stroke.
money: Set a maximum loss per round before you tee off. When you hit it, the betting stops for the day.
No presses or double-or-nothing when you are behind or angry.
Log money in every round so you see the real monthly number.
food: Alcohol: follow the weekly limit in the plan. All types raise flare risk, including wine.
Water: 2.5-3 L a day, more on golf and gym days.
Limit organ meats, shellfish, anchovy and sardine, sugary drinks and juice. Moderate red meat.
Good protein for building muscle: eggs, low-fat dairy, chicken, fish (not the high-purine ones), tofu and beans.
No vitamin C supplements for gout. If you use a painkiller in a flare, check the type with your doctor (aspirin is not a good choice for gout).
course: Pick clubs by your average carry, never your best shot.
Aim at the middle of the green. With a front pin, still play to the middle.
Between clubs, take the longer one. Arccos data: about 40% of amateur approaches finish short of the green and only about 5% go long.
Into the wind or uphill: at least one more club.
From the rough: expect less control - aim for the widest part of the green.
Your numbers come from mats and a net. Check them against the round log: if most misses are still short after 3 rounds, lower each club's number by 5 yards.
sun: Bangkok's UV index is often 11 or higher (extreme). The worst hours are 10:00-15:00. Swim and practise outdoors before 10:00 or after 16:00.
Sunscreen: broad-spectrum SPF 50 (30 at the very least), PA+++ or PA++++, water resistant. Apply 15 minutes before going out.
Swimming: 'water resistant' lasts 40 minutes in water, 'very water resistant' 80 minutes. Reapply after that and after towelling off.
Golf: reapply every 90 minutes to 2 hours - at the turn at the latest. Don't miss ears, neck, nose, the backs of your hands and the top of your head.
Wear: a wide-brim hat (or cap with a neck flap), UV sunglasses, UPF 50+ arm sleeves or long sleeves. In the pool: a UPF 50+ rash guard and UV-protected goggles.
Prefer 06:30 tee times: cooler, and most of the round is before peak UV. An 11:00 tee puts the whole round in the worst window.
Golfers get more skin cancer (Australian study: 27% had a diagnosis vs 7% of the public). Book a yearly skin check with a dermatologist and report any new or changing spot.
